links.comparator_used: Pre-implementation periods (ML development and external validation periods) with pharmacist-led prescription review but no ML warning or SMPOP process nodes; uncontrolled before-after comparison
links.outcome: Prescriber acceptance of pharmacist recommendations, length of stay, hospitalization and medication costs, ADRs
links.effect: Acceptance 43.95% (ML development period) and 40.63% (external validation period) vs 71.30% post-implementation (p<0.001); median length of stay 15 and 13 vs 7 days (p<0.001); median total costs 36,160 and 32,263 vs 20,843 RMB (p<0.001); median medication costs 8,795 and 7,848 vs 4,713 RMB (p<0.001); ADRs 0.19% and 0.4% vs 0.18% (p=0.095)
links.tradeoff: The ADR reduction was not statistically significant (p=0.095). The design is single-centre and before-after, with no concurrent control, so the effect of the ML warning cannot be separated from the pharmacist-led process redesign. The study reports no workload or latency data.
links.quote: After the introduction of ML model, this study shows that the acceptance rate of pharmacists' recommendations increased from 43.9% to 71.3%, indicating that the model enhanced the scientific rigor and credibility of pharmacists' advice.

design_hint: pharmacist-led review of ML prescription warnings
